PullRequest.Title: Copilot shim: rewrite the download line less often
PullRequest.Body:

Part of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#7531. Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9999 (from test plan item microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9852).

During the first-use install, `copilot` rewrote its "Downloading GitHub Copilot CLI... N MB of M MB (P%)" line every time the percentage changed, so a screen reader announced up to 100 updates. It now writes the line when the download starts and finishes, and otherwise at most every 5 seconds. The decision is a small pure function with a unit test.

### How to test
1. With Copilot CLI not installed and a screen reader running, run `copilot` in a terminal and answer `y`.
2. The download line updates about every 5 seconds instead of at every percent, and shows 100% when the download finishes.

### Validation
- `cargo fmt --check`: passed.
- `cargo test --locked` on Windows x64: passed (64 lib tests, including the new `download_progress_is_shown_at_the_start_the_end_and_every_interval`, plus the integration tests).
- `cargo test --locked` on Linux x64 (`rust:1.88` in Docker): passed.
- `cargo +1.88 clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`: passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Windows interactive first-use install with Copilot CLI absent
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Release resolution, checksum fetch, MSI download/write/hash, Authenticode verification, and msiexec complete sequentially. Console reporting is synchronous in each 64 KiB iteration, but the diff reduces actual stderr writes to start, completion, and at most once per five seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: HEAD latest release, GET checksums, and GET MSI
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three sequential logical requests per cold install.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same three-request sequence ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All block installation; their count and placement are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and write the temporary MSI while hashing each chunk
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file and approximately MSI_size/64 KiB writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical file and hash work occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each write is on the download critical path; unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rewrite the download line on stderr
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously start plus up to one write per integer percentage; now start/end plus at most one per five seconds. The decision still runs once per 64 KiB chunk.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundary was selected by percentage changes, up to roughly 101 writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Writes are synchronous, but the diff coalesces them. Downloads longer than about 8 minutes 20 seconds can exceed the old percentage-based maximum, still only at one write per five seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Verify the MSI signature and revocation state through WinVerifyTrust
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One identical verification ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before installation and is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One child per cold successful download.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same child and polling loop ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks successful completion; unchanged by progress throttling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: MSI size controls size/64 KiB reporter calls. Old terminal writes scaled with integer percentages; new writes scale with elapsed duration at one per five seconds plus start/end. Retained state is constant.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One serial download loop, three sequential logical HTTP requests, and one msiexec child. The diff adds no parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No download cache exists. An installed copilot.exe short-circuits all cold-install work. The new timestamp/byte tuple lives only for one reporter and does not alter caching or retries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the sole caller and chunk loop are directly traced, and all expensive boundaries remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: MSI size, speed, and terminal cost vary. Extremely slow downloads may produce more writes than the old cap, but the fixed five-second rate does not establish user-visible performance degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change coalesces terminal I/O and adds only a clock read per existing chunk callback, negligible beside network read, file write, and hashing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive invocation with Copilot already installed or installation disabled by policy
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Policy denial returns before reporter construction. Otherwise the expected executable/registration checks return before any progress callback when already installed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check the expected installed executable path
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One path check per allowed invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same immediate check and return occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines the warm short-circuit and is unchanged.

Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous and constant; no network request or subprocess.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The installed executable is the warm-state signal. No new persistent state or cache is added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the changed progress helper is unreachable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance effect on short-circuit paths.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed file and all diff pages. The PR rate-limits existing terminal rewrites without changing network, filesystem, verification, subprocess, concurrency, or retention costs; no finding was submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
